prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.40
  tan: 0.60
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” presents a rapid-change programme focused on cutting immigration, taxes and regulation; overhauling public services; expanding domestic energy; and constitutional shifts to assert UK sovereignty. The party frames the plan as an alternative to Conservatives and Labour, aiming to “take back control” of borders, money and laws.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration and “stop the boats.”
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 to “make work pay.”
- Scrap Net Zero policies and unlock UK oil and gas to cut bills.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential visas; create a Department of Immigration.
- Detain and deport illegal entrants; leave the ECHR if needed; process offshore; bar asylum from safe countries.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals; restrict student dependants; five‑year residency for benefits.
- Employer immigration tax (higher NI for foreign hires, with exemptions).

Government waste
- Stop Bank of England interest on QE reserves; 5% departmental efficiency drive; cut EU‑era rules; halve foreign aid; improve HMRC collection.

Economy (personal)
- Lift income tax start to £20k; higher rate from £70k.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and green levies.
- Big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT‑free tourist shopping.
- IHT abolished below £2m; 20% rate above.

Economy (business)
- Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15%.
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset with 4% online delivery tax.
- Looser employment rules; faster planning; major tax simplification.

NHS
- Zero basic‑rate income tax for NHS/care staff for 3 years; expand UK training and write off fees with service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks.
- Efficiency drives; pharmacy‑first approach; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.

Net Zero/energy
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale trials.
- Expand nuclear SMRs and other technologies.

Policing and justice
- 40,000 extra officers; zero‑tolerance approach; more stop and search; end DE&I roles.
- Increase justice budget; redefine hate crime; 10,000 new prison places; mandatory life for repeat violent offenders.

Education
- “Patriotic” curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees.
- Scrap interest on student loans; tougher university standards; protect free speech; expand PRUs; offer 2‑year degrees.

Welfare
- Stronger work requirements (two‑strike rule); face‑to‑face assessments.

Brexit/sovereignty
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare TCA renegotiation; distance from EU defence ties.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; new justice bill; veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform.

Housing
- Fast‑track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; protect leaseholders.

Families
- Transferable marriage allowance (aiming at 25%); front‑load child benefit for ages 1–4; single‑sex spaces; tackle social media harms.

Transport/utilities
- Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs/most 20mph zones; invest in existing roads/rails.
- New ownership model: 50% public, 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges.

Agriculture/fishing
- Boost farm budget; scrap climate‑linked subsidies; protect country sports; curb supermarket power; buy British.
- Restrict foreign access to UK waters; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing and fleets.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax avoidance in care; pension reforms; fix Mineworkers’ scheme.

Constitution/culture
- Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Reject WHO treaty/WEF/CBDC; replace Equalities Act; free speech bill; scrap BBC licence fee; national holidays; anti‑corruption unit.

Funding (party estimates)
- Annual savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from extra growth = £160bn.
- Annual costs: ~£141bn.

TEXT_E:
Labour’s 2024 manifesto sets out a fiscally responsible plan to “stop the chaos,” restore stability and rebuild Britain around five national missions, underpinned by strong foundations in national security, secure borders and economic stability. Fiscal rules require the current budget to balance and debt to fall as a share of GDP by year five. Labour pledges no rises in National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates or VAT; it will fund plans by abolishing non-dom status, closing avoidance loopholes (including carried interest and offshore trusts) and modernising HMRC.

Five missions
1) Kickstart economic growth: A pro-business, pro-worker industrial strategy with an independent Industrial Strategy Council; a £7.3bn National Wealth Fund to crowd in private investment; planning reform and 1.5m homes; deeper devolution with Local Growth Plans; a New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; day-one rights; stronger enforcement; minimum wage based on living costs and without age bands). Cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; retain full expensing; replace business rates; 10-year infrastructure strategy and a National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; bus franchising/municipal ownership; EV charging rollout and restore 2030 ICE phase-out; fix 1m potholes annually; nationwide gigabit and 5G by 2030; a Regulatory Innovation Office and binding rules for frontier AI; support SMEs (late payments, procurement, British Business Bank reform). Reduce net migration by linking visas to skills plans and tougher enforcement; merge Jobcentre Plus and the National Careers Service; a youth guarantee for 18–21s.

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower: Zero-carbon electricity by 2030 via doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, quadrupling offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen and long-duration storage; back nuclear (extend existing, deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C, support SMRs); maintain a strategic gas reserve; no new oil and gas exploration licences (manage existing fields). Create Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and scale local power; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; British Jobs Bonus to anchor supply chains; green finance leadership and a carbon border mechanism. Restore nature and clean up rivers with tougher water regulation; support British farmers; strengthen animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets: A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (thousands more officers/PCSOs); new Respect Orders; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers and tougher shoplifting rules; halve knife crime with mandatory interventions and bans on machetes/zombie knives and online sales; Young Futures hubs; specialist rape units and fast-track courts; higher policing standards and vetting; a fraud strategy; expand prison capacity and cut reoffending; Hillsborough Law and action on historical injustices.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity: 3,000 school-based nurseries; 6,500 new teachers; free breakfast clubs in every primary; curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion; mental health support in every school; Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform the Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; improve HE access and funding; broaden access to arts/sport and a football regulator; a Race Equality Act, disability/ethnicity pay-gap reporting, a full ban on conversion practices, and modernised gender recognition law.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends) and shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver the New Hospitals Programme; upgrade the NHS app; safer maternity care; more GPs, continuity of care and modern booking; expand pharmacist prescribing and direct referrals; Neighbourhood Health Centres; a Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments, contract reform, supervised toothbrushing); a National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 extra mental health staff and Young Futures hubs; robust public health measures (smoking/vaping, junk-food ads, energy drinks, online/gambling harms); tackle health inequalities, prioritise women’s health and aim to end new HIV cases by 2030.

Serving the country and foreign policy: An independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons rules and ban MPs’ paid consultancy; Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80) and consult on replacement; votes at 16; reset relations with devolved governments; uphold the ECHR. Unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review on a path to 2.5% of GDP; defence industrial strategy; steadfast support for Ukraine (including using frozen Russian assets); AUKUS; pragmatic China policy. Make Brexit work with a better EU relationship (no single market/customs union/FoM), sector deals (e.g., veterinary, MRAs), and a security pact. Targeted trade deals aligned to the industrial strategy; lead a Clean Power Alliance; rebuild international development capacity and restore 0.7% when fiscal space allows.

First steps for change
- Economic stability with tough spending rules
- Cut NHS waits with 40,000 extra weekly appointments
- New Border Security Command
- Create Great British Energy
- Crack down on antisocial behaviour
- Recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_E aligns more closely with this profile.
